answer_text:
Since \(X,Y\) are i.i.d. standard normal, their joint distribution is rotationally symmetric. Let the polar angle of \((X,Y)\) be \(\Theta\). Then \(\Theta\) is uniform on \([0,2\pi)\).

We need

\[
P(X>0 \mid X>Y)
=
\frac{P(X>0,\; X>Y)}{P(X>Y)}.
\]

In terms of the angle \(\theta\):

- \(X>0 \iff \cos\theta>0 \iff \theta\in(-\pi/2,\pi/2)\).
- \(X>Y \iff \cos\theta>\sin\theta \iff \theta\in(-3\pi/4,\pi/4)\).

Thus,

\[
P(X>Y)=\frac{\pi}{2\pi}=\frac12.
\]

The intersection is

\[
(-\pi/2,\pi/4),
\]

which has length

\[
\frac{\pi}{4}-\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{3\pi}{4}.
\]

So

\[
P(X>0,\; X>Y)=\frac{3\pi/4}{2\pi}=\frac38.
\]

Therefore,

\[
P(X>0 \mid X>Y)
=
\frac{3/8}{1/2}
=
\frac34.
\]

\[
\boxed{0.75}
\]
